text:
Ben Kindel is 19, in his second NHL season, and already playing 17:43 a night for a Penguins team that has lost eight of its last ten. The early-career numbers say he belongs: 11 points in 21 games is 0.52 a game, well above the 0.37 that forwards picked in his draft range have typically managed in their first full seasons.

The points could be better, and not because of him. Pittsburgh has scored 11.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Kindel on the ice, one of the biggest shortfalls in the league, and his own shooting is at 9.3%. He has one goal in his last ten games on 2.8 expected goals (the quality of chances). That gap tends to close.

The worry is at the other end: the Penguins get 48% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, 5.2 points worse than without him. That's a teenager taking real minutes on a struggling team. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his zone entries last season (carry-ins on 56%). We'd watch whether the ice time keeps climbing through the losing.
